case_name: The New Keyboard — Innocent Failed Login
description: User with a new mechanical keyboard (different switches) makes 3 typing errors before entering the correct password. The pattern is: error, quick correction, successful login, normal 8-hour activity.
devil_advocate: Maria Garcia is an attacker who stole her credentials and is testing the new keyboard as an alibi to explain the brute force errors
devil_refutation: The attacker hypothesis does not explain why the timing is human (not automated), why there are 8 hours of normal post-login activity, or why the keyboard was requested 3 days earlier. The benign explanation is simpler.

peirce_expected.firstness: Three failed login attempts followed by success
peirce_expected.secondness: Failed attempts have variable human timing (6s, 7s). Post-login there are 8 hours of normal activity with no anomalies. The new keyboard was formally requested.
peirce_expected.thirdness: This is a legitimate user adapting to a new keyboard. The typing errors are physical (tactile adaptation), not brute force. The benign hypothesis explains all artifacts without contradictions.

why_not_malice: The errors have a verifiable physical explanation. There is no second anomaly (exfiltration, escalation, unusual hours).
